title: Technical rapid onboarding kit and threat clarity brief
author: Marcus Lee
content:
Overview:

This kit is a compact, technical sales enablement artifact intended for platform engineers, CTOs, and sales engineering teams running a 2–6 week value sprint (pilot). It combines concise positioning and messaging, a competitive signal brief, a pitch outline for technical decision-makers, pricing scenarios for pilot-to-production conversion, a short case study template, and a focused security FAQ designed for initial prospect diligence.

Goals and audience:
- Primary audience: platform engineers, lead SREs, CTOs evaluating inference platforms.
- Secondary audience: sales engineers, solutions architects, procurement leads.
- Pilot goal: validate 3 production metrics (latency, token cost, and reliability) on representative workload within 2–6 weeks.

What success looks like (pilot acceptance criteria):
1) Latency: median 95th percentile request latency <= target (customer-provided baseline or 150ms for short-text generation).
2) Cost: measured per-token cost reduction or parity vs baseline within expected quantization/batching uplift (target: <=1.2x baseline for first-pass integration).
3) Reliability: >=99.5% successful calls over a 7-day window under the pilot traffic profile.
4) Quality: automated evals on a shortlist of 200 prompts must show no more than X% regression on defined metrics (to be agreed with customer; default 5%).

Positioning and core messaging (elevator + tech hooks):
- Elevator: "Redwood Inference delivers predictable inference economics and strong latency SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so engineering teams ship LLM features without re-architecting for each model or region."
- Tech hooks to use in conversations: unified runtime, automated batching and KV caching, per-route token and latency telemetry, model variant fallback policy, private deployment controls (VPC/KMS), deterministic autoscaling for reserved capacity.

Competitive brief (signals to surface during evaluation):
- Strengths to emphasize:
  - Production-first runtime (continuous batching + KV cache) that reduces per-token cost without heavy client engineering.
  - Straightforward private deployment path: VPC + on-prem bundle with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
  - Built-in rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic rollback when quality gates fail.
- Common competitor claims and rebuttals:
  - Competitor: "Lowest API latency" — Rebuttal: measure with our synthetic latency harness and look at 95p under customer traffic shape; Redwood provides transparent per-route breakdown and fallback strategies to preserve SLAs.
  - Competitor: "Cheaper at scale" — Rebuttal: Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization profiles) and telemetry-driven cost analysis close that gap while preserving quality guarantees.

Pitch deck / demo outline for a 20–30 minute technical session:
1) Slide 1: One-line value + customer logo examples
2) Slide 2: Short architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private lanes) with routing policies
3) Slide 3: Key metrics we will measure in the pilot (latency, cost per 1K tokens, error rate, eval quality)
4) Slide 4: Pilot plan and timeline (see next section)
5) Slide 5: Security & compliance summary (KMS, audit logs, network options)
6) Slide 6: Pricing scenarios and conversion path to Reserved Capacity or Private Deployment
7) Slide 7: Short case study + next steps and asks from customer

Rapid pilot plan (2–6 week template):
Week 0 (pre-commit): scoping session, data/sample prompts, access and NDA.
Week 1: onboarding — API keys, baseline tests, instrument telemetry (SDK or curl), and a first synthetic throughput/latency run.
Week 2: integration — prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and autotuning recommended batching/quantization profile.
Week 3: production-style load run and quality evals; surface cost and latency dashboards.
Week 4: finalize go/no-go metrics and handoff plan; prepare proposal to convert to Dedicated or Private.
Optional extension (weeks 5–6): region failover and long-tail regression checks.

Pilot onboarding checklist (engineer-facing):
- Agreement/NDA and pilot scope signed
- Sample prompt set (200–1000 examples) uploaded or shared
- Network connectivity plan (hosted vs VPC peering or VPN)
- API key + route-level config created by Redwood SE
- Telemetry ingestion: enable per-route tracing and token accounting
- Baseline metrics captured (customer incumbent endpoint or expectation)

Sample API call (curl) to include in demo: 
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model": "rwd-3b", "input": "Summarize the following user message: ...", "max_tokens": 64, "stream": false}'

Pricing guidance (scenarios & negotiation levers):
- Pilot pricing: trial credits + short-term usage tier (no commitment). Default scope: up to 1M tokens free for 2–6 week pilots for qualifying prospects.
- Conversion paths:
  - Reserved Capacity (Dedicated): monthly commitment with SLA and unit discount (typical discounts 30–50% vs hosted on-demand).
  - Private (VPC/On-prem): platform license + support and optional managed services fee; pricing varies by core footprint and retention requirements.
- Negotiation levers to protect margin: minimal committed run-rate for production conversion, phased discounting tied to latency and error SLO attainment, migration service fees for on-prem packaging.

Quick economics table (example text representation):
| Scenario | On-demand hosted unit cost | Estimated monthly tokens | Estimated monthly cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Pilot (2–6w) | $0.0008 / token | 1,000,000 | $800 (often credit-covered) | Short evaluation, no SLA
| Production small (Dedicated) | $0.00045 / token | 50,000,000 | $22,500 | Reserved discount + autoscale cap
| Private (license + infra) | N/A | N/A | Custom | Includes licensing, infra, support

Case study template (for handoff to CS when pilot succeeds):
- Customer: [name] (industry)
- Use case and sample flows integrated during pilot
- Baseline metrics and pilot results (latency, cost, reliability, quality evals)
- Deployment choice recommended (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and rationale
- Next steps and engineering handoff items (timeline, SOW estimate)

Security FAQ (concise answers for early diligence):
Q: How is customer data protected in hosted deployments?
A: Data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest. We support per-customer keying via KMS (cloud or customer-managed HSM for Private). Audit logs capture model invocations and admin actions.

Q: Can we run inference on-prem or in our VPC?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-prem installer for air-gapped environments. We provide integration guidance for KMS and logging, and an optional managed service layer for installs.

Q: What logs and telemetry are available to customers?
A: Per-route token accounting, per-request latency and error traces, model versioning, and KV cache hit metrics. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs using secure streaming connectors (S3/CloudWatch/Events).

Q: How do you support compliance and audits?
A: We provide artifacts for SOC2 readiness, help integrate with customer audit processes, and can support contractual data residency and retention terms for Private deployments.

Q: What mitigations exist for model drift or quality regressions?
A: Redwood Optimize includes eval suites and regression alerts tethered to prompt sets. Rollouts support automatic rollback or fallback to a verified model variant when quality or latency thresholds are breached.

Sales engineering playbook: recommended talking points and asks:
- Initial ask of prospect: provide a representative production prompt set, an incumbent baseline, and a short list of critical failure modes.
- Instrumentation ask: enable tracing on the first route we test and allow SE to configure a temporary route-level policy for throttling and batching.
- Risk/compensation: propose a short SLA tied to pilot outcomes and reserve conversion credits toward the first month of Dedicated if conversion occurs.

Appendix: links / attachable artifacts
- Attach: sample prompt-set template (CSV), synthetic latency harness script (bash), local eval runner (python snippet), and a short architecture diagram (SVG).
- Example eval runner command: python eval_runner.py --prompts prompts.csv --model rwd-3b --results results.json

Ownership and escalation
- SE owner: assign named Redwood SE on pilot kickoff.
- Renewal lead: AE + Solutions Architect to prepare proposal 1 week prior to pilot end.
- Technical escalation: Eng-Platform oncall for Private/VPC issues; Eng-Serving-Runtime for kernel or performance anomalies.

Notes and constraints
- This kit is intentionally compact for rapid consumption; customize the SLO values and pricing numbers for each prospect.
- Always validate any cost estimate against the latest unit economics from the Pricing and Product team (linked in related_pages).
